newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks continue bull run.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks continue bull run.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares charged higher on Tuesday, shrugging off the country's continuing crisis over a crippling strike by civil servants now in its third week.
The key industrial index rose 1.2 percent -- or 68.17 points -- to reach yet another a record 5,917.33.

"The market is looking very firm. The ongoing wrangle between civil servants and the government has had no effect. People are looking at fundamentals which are right," one broker said, pointing at softening short-term trading rates on the local money market as well as a fall in annual inflation to 22 percent in July from 28 percent in January.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Tuesday, bankers FMB surged 200 cents to 3,100, Barclays jumped 110 cents to 2,010, pharmaceutical firm Caps rose 50 cents to 200, plate glass firm PG gained 40 cents to 480 and cement producer Porthold climbed 25 cents to 1,125.

Also among the winners, multi-industrial group Radar and packaging firm Hunyani gained 20 cents each to 170 and 280 respectively while clothing retailer Truworths at 650 and finance group Finhold at 640 both rose 15 cents.
Conglomerate TA Holdings was the only loser of the day, shedding 10 cents to 130.
Minings were a bit subdued with copper producer Mhangura firming two cents to 22 and Falgold adding five cents to 175. The mining index slipped a marginal 0.32 points to 1,317.31.
